liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): The performance is well jammed, featuring notable keyboard work from Keith; The performance is described as blisteringly hot, causing the reviewer to bang their feet [9][12]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Bob forgets the lyrics during the performance of this song [13]
- **Other One (1st verse only)** (1 review): The keyboard sound in the jam sequence is memorable and tasty [17]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Jerry leaves out some of the verses during the performance [13]

## The recordings

- **gd74-07-29.matrix.chappell.29482.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 187 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: The matrix recording features a good mix of crowd and music [16]
- **gd74-07-29.moore.weiner.gdADT20.17968.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 188 min; rated 3.86/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: The audience recording provides ambience missing from the clinical soundboard version [11]
- **gd1974-07-29.107990.mtx.seamons.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 188 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1974-07-29.akgd1000e.moore.berger.106066.flac24**: audience recording; 23 songs; 188 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Jerry dominates the first set, particularly on Scarlet Begonias and Cumberland Blues [9]
- This marks the band's first appearance at the Capitol Centre [11]
- Someone shot off an M-80 firecracker during To Lay Me Down [14]
- Peggy-O was played near the very end, after Wharf Rat and Around & Around [15]
- The reviewer considers this show and Louisville the best on the site [12]
- This recording sounds much better than the muddy June 30, 1974 show [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-07-29.matrix.chappell.29482.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Jerry Moore and Teddy Goodbear; transferred by Chris Chappell; source: Matrix [1]. Also: Chris Chappell edited and transferred the matrix from existing soundboard and audience sources [1]
- **gd74-07-29.moore.weiner.gdADT20.17968.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Mark Cohen and Noah Weiner; source: Audience Recording [3]. Also: Jerry Moore recorded the show using expensive taping equipment in 1974 [18]
- **gd1974-07-29.107990.mtx.seamons.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: SBD (107756) + AUD (106066) [5]. Also: Charlie Miller transferred the soundboard, while Jerry Moore recorded the audience portion [5]
- **gd1974-07-29.akgd1000e.moore.berger.106066.flac24**: taped by Jerry Moore; transferred by Rob Berger; source: aud>akg d1000e's>sony tc-152sd (2)tdk c-120sd's**, dolby b cassettes [2]
